description: Ad-hoc filter behaviour of the relations tooltip footer against the LGTM stack's own service graph, which Tempo's metrics-generator publishes with real client/server labels. Sibling of echarts-relations-adhoc-filters on the dev Grafana; same six panels, a topology small enough to hold in your head. Grafana and Prometheus sit in the middle, user is a pure origin, elasticsearch and grafana-assistant-app are pure destinations, and prometheus calls itself.

options.content:
# Ad-hoc filters, one behaviour per panel

Pin a tooltip — **click** a node or a link — and the footer offers **Filter on this value**,
**Filter out this value**, and a **Filter for …** button per non-endpoint label. They write into
the **Ad hoc filters** variable at the top, which Prometheus injects into every query's metric
selector, so the whole dashboard narrows on the click.

Everything below is about one question: **which label key does an endpoint go out under, and is it
offered at all?** The contract's own `source`/`target` is a *topology carrier* — it says which mark
connects to which, not that the datasource has ever heard of a label called `source`. A filter built
straight from the frame is `source="elasticsearch"`, which matches zero series and silently empties the
dashboard.

| Panel | What it isolates | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | the `filterable` gate, and a **derived** node taking the edges' opt-in | `resolveFilters`, `markFilterable` |
| 3 | the same panel with the gate off — no buttons anywhere | `resolveFilters` |
| 4 | **direction**: a destination-only node asserts its *target* key | `toNodeFilterLabels` |
| 5 | why the fallback exists — a node override with nothing to bind to | `markFilterable` |
| 6 | two levels, **per-edge** key recovery, and a middle node deduping to one key | `aliasEndpointKeys`, `toNodeFilterLabels` |
| 7 | the last resort, for a query that destroyed its own key | `addRelationsFilterConfig` |

Panels 2–6 configure **nothing**. Only panel 7 sets a key by hand, and only because its query threw
the original away. Clear the variable between experiments — a stale `!=` chip looks like a bug in the
panel.

**The topology is tiny and every role is in it**: `user` only ever calls (a pure origin, and a `virtual_node`), `elasticsearch` and `grafana-assistant-app` are only ever called, `grafana` and `prometheus` sit in the middle, and `prometheus` calls itself. Every edge is produced by these five containers doing their normal work, so **a quiet stack is a thin graph** — open a few dashboards to give Tempo something to measure.

panels.title: The gate is on — and every node here is derived
panels.description:
`sum by (client, server)` — the pair the reader recognises, so nothing is configured here at all and the filters still go out under the datasource's own keys (`ENDPOINT_LABEL_PAIRS`). Standard **Filterable** is set once in the Fields tab, which is why any button appears at all (`resolveFilters`).

The response is **edges only**, so no node has a field of its own: each is a mark the response only implied. Pin one anyway and it offers filters, taken from the edges that named it (`markFilterable` → `RelationsMarks.endpointsFilterable`). Pin an edge for the grouped pair, and `connection_type` for a button of its own.

panels.title: The same panel with Filterable off — no buttons at all
panels.description:
Identical query, identical marks; **Filterable** cleared in the Fields tab. The footer offers no filter button on any mark, node or edge — a filter written under a key the datasource cannot answer either does nothing or empties the dashboard, so the panel offers nothing instead.

Data links are **not** gated the same way: a link is the field's own config, not a claim about the query. This panel has none to show, but `per-mark-tooltip-links.json` does.

panels.title: Direction — a destination-only node asserts its target key
panels.description:
The bug this fixes: which key can carry a node's name is a property of the **topology**, not of the node. Pin **elasticsearch** — it is never a client — and "Filter on this value" asserts the *target* key, not `client="elasticsearch"`, which would match no series at all. No key mapping could have fixed that: the key was right and the direction was wrong.

Pin **grafana**, which is at both ends of something, and it asserts the source key instead — `client=x AND server=x` is self-loops, and there is no ad-hoc filter for "either endpoint".

"Filter out this value" negates **both** keys on either node. That is deliberate and asymmetric: a `topk` re-ranks the moment the filter applies, so negating one direction alone lets the node reappear at the other end (`NodeFilterLabels.negate`).

panels.title: Why the fallback exists — a node override with nothing to bind to
panels.description:
Same query, with a `byName` override clearing **Filterable** on the `elasticsearch` node — and it makes **no difference**: pin that node and both buttons are still there. This is not a bug in the override, it is the reason `markFilterable` has a fallback at all.

A node override needs the node to *be* a field, which is what the derived-node pre-pass provides — and that needs the `panelPluginTransformations` feature. **This Grafana is 13.1 and does not have it**, so every node here is a mark the response only implied, with no field for an override to land on and none to carry `filterable`. So the node takes the **edges'** answer instead, which is the honest authority: a node's filters are written under the endpoint keys, and those are the edges' dimensions.

Gating on the node's own absent field is what left a service-graph panel offering filters on every link and none at all on its nodes. To turn a node off *here* you turn the whole panel off — panel 3. The dev-Grafana sibling (`echarts-relations-adhoc-filters`) runs a build that has the feature, and there the same override does bind.

panels.title: Two levels in one frame, each filtering under its own keys

targets.expr:
sum by (source, target, stack, client) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__range]),
    "source", "$1", "stack", "(.*)"),
  "target", "$1", "client", "(.*)")
)
or
sum by (source, target, client, server) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__range]),
    "source", "$1", "client", "(.*)"),
  "target", "$1", "server", "(.*)")
)

panels.title: The last resort — a query that destroyed its own key
panels.description:
`sum by (source, target) (label_replace(…))` with the originals **dropped** from the outer aggregation. Nothing can recover them, so this is the one case the per-mark setting exists for: **Fields → Ad-hoc filters** sets `client` / `server` as the keys the endpoints go out under.

It is **field config**, not a panel option, so a panel joining two queries can answer per edge — and it keeps its *defaults* editor, because one response usually does group by one pair and "every mark" is worth saying once. Compare panel 6, which needs none of this.

targets.expr:
sum by (source, target) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__range]),
    "source", "$1", "client", "(.*)"),
  "target", "$1", "server", "(.*)")
)
